text:
If you’re hoping for a dry Burlington sunset, keep expectations modest. It’ll stay cloudy through sunset at 7:27, with the better chance for rain arriving this evening and continuing overnight. The forecast carries a 90 percent rain chance, with periods of heavier rain and a few embedded thunderstorms, but the forecasters acknowledge the steadiest rain could miss us to the north or south. South winds will also ramp up on the lake, peaking between 8 and midnight, with waves building to 4 to 6 feet, so tonight is no time to be out on the water.

Tomorrow starts with a high around 80 and some breaks of sun, but showers and thunderstorms remain likely, especially during the afternoon. The models are fairly close on the temperature, but they keep the rain signal strong, so I’d plan on a warm day with interruptions rather than a washout. Enjoy the sunset from shore if you’re out, then be home before the heavier rain and strongest lake winds arrive.
